issues.legal_issue: An ex parte appellate judgment must be set aside and the appeal reheard when the absent respondent had sufficient cause for not appearing.
material_facts: The appellant was the principal respondent in a second appeal before the High Court.
The second appeal was allowed ex parte when the appellant did not appear at the hearing.
The appellant said he had not been served with notice of the second appeal, and the Supreme Court found that he had sufficient cause for not appearing.
issues.conclusion: The ex parte judgment was set aside and the second appeal was remanded to the High Court for disposal according to law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that an ex parte appellate judgment should be set aside and the appeal remitted when the absent party had sufficient cause for nonappearance. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_challenges_ex_parte_appellate_jud: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an appellate judgment made ex parte against a respondent.
predicates.respondent_had_sufficient_cause_for_abse: The respondent had sufficient cause for not appearing at the hearing.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an ex parte appellate judgment and the respondent had sufficient cause for absence, the judgment is set aside and the appeal is remanded.
